# Best open-ear earbuds for running

Prices below come from the reviews, so check the current price before you buy.

| Pick | Best for | Price | Battery | Water rating |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | Best overall, sound quality | $199 (was $299) | ~7 hrs, 19.5-27 with case | IPX4 |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | Maximum awareness (bone conduction) | $180 list; $125 at some retailers | 12 hrs | IP55 |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | Long runs, rain | $200 | 10 hrs, 40 with case | IP57 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | Best value, sound for running | $99 at Amazon | Long | IP54 |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | Budget ear-hook | $79.99 at Amazon | 10 hrs, 42 with case | IP55 |
| **JLab Flex Open / Soundpeats PearlClip Pro** | Cheapest way to try the style | ~$40-50 | ~7-7.5 hrs | IPX5 or higher |

## My top picks

- **Bose Ultra Open ($199):** Runner's World ranks it best overall, and WIRED calls it the best sound in a clip-on. Each bud has a physical button, which is easier than touch controls mid-run. The downsides are IPX4 water resistance, so skip them for heavy rain, and volume that can be low in loud traffic. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** This is the pick if hearing your surroundings is your top priority. It's a neckband with bone conduction plus small air-conduction speakers for bass, and it has physical controls. The band can interfere with long hair and winter hats. RTINGS found the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz has the tougher rating and multi-device pairing. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- **Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200):** WIRED's top overall pick. Its 10-hour battery and IP57 rating (the reviewer submerged them) suit marathon training and rainy runs. It's pricey, and Runner's World notes the volume could be better. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Nothing Ear (Open) (~$99):** SoundGuys picked it as best open-ear overall and best workout earbud for running. It has strong bass for this category, a parametric EQ, and an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [SoundGuys workout list](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** It's a secure ear-hook design with IP55 and a 10-hour battery. [Buy at Soundcore (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)

## Notes

- **AeroFit 2 pricing doesn't match across sources.** Dealectric lists $129.99 at Soundcore, or about $104 with code AFSC20, which is for full-price items. SoundGuys shows $79.99 at Amazon. Compare before using the code.
- **Budget price conflict:** Runner's World lists the JLab Flex Open at $40 in its listing but says $50 in the text. It's the cheapest way to find out whether you like the clip-on style.
- **Safety:** Open-ear designs help you hear traffic, but they don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume moderate.
- **Bose may release a new model soon.** Runner's World says Bose plans new open-ear earbuds within the next month, so you may see price drops on the current pair.

I only have review-page links for most of these, not direct store links. Each review's retailer buttons (Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, REI) go to the purchase page.

If you tell me your budget and whether you run in rain, wear glasses or hats, or have long hair, I can narrow this to one pick.
